caption:
Women's leadership share at India Inc has fallen from 20% to 16.7% — reported by Business Today on 10 September 2026, from the 11th Best Companies for Women in India study.

Read where that drop happens. Not at the door. At the rung where authority gets assigned.

Getting into the room is an access problem. Being treated as the authority in the room is a presence problem. Most qualified people solve the first and are never told the second exists. So they speak, are passed over, and hear their own idea repeated back by someone with better bearing.

Bearing is trainable. Tone is trainable. Calculated silence is trainable. Thirty-five years of command taught Colonel Suhag that authority is not granted by the org chart — it is read off the person holding the floor.

The data is a headwind. It is not a verdict. Train for the moment that decides.

topic.title: Women's leadership share at India Inc falls 20% to 16.7%
topic.angle: Lumina's audience is qualified professionals who get overlooked, and this data shows the overlooking worsening precisely at the rung where authority is assigned — the gap between getting into the room and being treated as the authority in it.
topic.why_now: Business Today published the finding on 10 September 2026 from the 11th Best Companies for Women in India study, so it is roughly a week old and still circulating before data posts read as stale.

rationale: A stark two-number typographic visual carries the statistic without decoration, matching the brand's plainspoken authority and keeping the caption's focus on the presence gap rather than the chart.
